title: Automated Proof-of-Location Framework for Dedicated Nodes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable, auditable framework that proves physical/geographic placement and isolation of Dedicated capacity nodes and packages tamper-evident evidence bundles for customer attestations. This ticket covers collector agents, signed manifests, retention enforcement hooks, and an automated reporter that produces time-windowed compliance packages suitable for regulators and SOC-style audits.
acceptance_criteria: Collector agent deployed on Dedicated hosts produces signed location manifests (node metadata + geo-resolution + time) and uploads to durable evidence store
Manifest format is versioned and includes KMS-signed root hash, per-chunk SHA256 hashes, and a human-readable summary for auditors
Retention policies applied to evidence store honor tenant-specific retention/freeze windows and support WORM export for regulatory holds
Console exposes a read-only Evidence Viewer per tenant with RBAC-limited download links and audit logging
Automated nightly reporter composes a compliance package (manifest + chain-of-custody log + verification checklist) and stores export with provenance headers
End-to-end test exists that validates manifest signature, hash chain, and retrieval for a sample tenant in a dedicated region
tasks: Spec: define manifest schema and signature envelope (owner: Marcus)
Collector: implement systemd agent + lightweight daemon to gather metadata and TTLed geolocation (owner: Lina Ortega)
Storage: S3 bucket lifecycle + retention enforcement + export hook (owner: Platform Infra)
KMS integration: envelope signing via HSM-backed KMS and rotation plan (owner: Security)
Reporter: scheduled composition job that bundles evidence into signed archives and pushes to customer export endpoint (owner: Marcus)
Console: Evidence Viewer and signed-download endpoint with RBAC checks (owner: Product)
E2E tests and demo runbook for audit team (owner: QA)
Release notes and runbook for on-call operators (owner: SRE)

decisions: Use asymmetric KMS signing (HSM-backed) for manifests rather than symmetric MACs to simplify public verification for customers
Store raw collector events for 90 days encrypted-at-rest; generate and export signed attestations on demand or on nightly schedule
Evidence bundles will include a verification.txt that lists per-file SHA256 and the signing key id and timestamp to support external auditors
Retention enforcement is implemented at storage layer with S3 object lock + lifecycle and an application-enforced policy gate for tenant overrides
